name: Unidentified eggs or small insects on tender flush
distinction: Eggs and small insects can include beneficial organisms. Confirm the organism, plant symptoms, and infestation trend rather than treating eggs alone as psyllid.
action: Use the stage guide, record the observation, and seek local confirmation if identification remains uncertain.

name: Trunk injury or another collar disorder
distinction: Gum or bark damage alone does not establish a Phytophthora diagnosis. Record its position relative to the soil line, drainage conditions, recent injury, and canopy decline.
action: Do not scrape or paint the trunk until the cause is reasonably confirmed.

name: Root stress, disease, or another deficiency
distinction: Leaf yellowing can have multiple causes. New versus old leaf position, vein pattern, soil conditions, irrigation, and root health matter before naming a deficiency.
action: Record the pattern and obtain appropriate local soil or leaf-test advice before applying a nutrient product.
